context_protocol.selection_binding: server-normalized relevant requested filters/project set/report month plus purpose included in collection fingerprint; no arbitrary resolver/SQL/ref supplied by client
context_protocol.collection_revision: all scope-contributing relation generations + current actor mapping/epoch + fixed selection; no TopN/page-size based authorization manifest
context_protocol.plan: domain trusted QueryBindings; SQL predicate before aggregates, pagination and filter options; actual single object capabilities checked separately
context_protocol.writes: /me requires_context never enables write; only current exact object/collection checked capability enables UI. Server always reauthorizes after domain locks, regardless client capability/revision.
context_protocol.failure: ordinary denied action may be a deny block; invalid state/PDP/DB is whole request failure; do not cache old allow
context_protocol.provenance: existing framework extended with domain object/collection validators; actual object dependencies separately keyed, no per-resource collapse
context_protocol.resolver: Existing domain GET or read-only POST explicitly supporting view=authorization. Fixed server resolver registry; named live user; locator+authorization_context only, no business fact SQL. No generic resource/action/ref request. Child-specific writes consume the exact child context, never parent allow.
context_protocol.query_binding: Project family: derived subquery selects project_id and four labelled SQL EXISTS/Boolean columns with .table; bind columns to Cerbos SQLAlchemy QueryBindings, then project_id IN (SELECT project_id WHERE policy predicate). No raw EXISTS binding and no uncorrelated added FROM. Apply before aggregate/sort/page. Owner/source families use their real derived columns.
context_protocol.internal_wire_conversion: Internal Ref.kind is flat closed_internal_context_kinds. HTTP uses kind=object,object_type=Ref.kind for every child; explicit server serializer and generated TS enum, no second wire protocol.
context_protocol.proof_requirements: All scopes, including all/all_projects, require actual trusted typed domain_context matching registered context kinds/ref/selector/revision. Bare object_id+revision is insufficient. Definitions with query_attributes need real attrs/bindings. Only explicitly context_only definitions can omit bindings; object existence/topology is still checked.
context_protocol.read_consistency: Batch read uses one short independent REPEATABLE READ snapshot for actor, Grant rows, all parent relations and business projection/authorization facts, without explicit domain or actor locks. READ COMMITTED multi-query stitched hashes are not a proof. If streaming, validate again per existing publication/chunk protocol. Root-issued ReadSnapshot marks this RR transaction; ordinary unlocked SysUser must not masquerade as locked_user. All fact SQL and DTO projection complete inside the snapshot before returning; do not return only proof and later query in RC.
context_protocol.write_consistency: Parse complete target topology; acquire every domain lock in stable order, then one live actor SHARE (and any truly mutated users at final required strength); revalidate all contexts inside same transaction. Receipt move stabilizes old+new project then child UPDATE; project SHARE alone cannot stabilize child parent. No connection switch in callbacks and no more domain lock after actor.
context_protocol.multi_context: All dependencies resolved together. Never loop (domain lock→actor) per object. Documents spanning projects use complete union of locks or one read snapshot, retain each (resource,context) separately, no field/scope union.

context_protocol.action_context_validation: Core validates exact action-context kind/purpose/selector shape, then domain resolves the exact entry contract and mandatory evidence. Resource-level kinds are descriptive unions only, never sufficient authorization. Project resolver may emit allow only for actions whose actual context is this project; child-only actions remain requires_context until child resolver.
context_protocol.policy_subjects: ResolvedContext carries actual carrier_ref/revision and subjects keyed by exact resource. First choose entry binding conditions/complete-contract alternatives from actual input/object. Expand only chosen (carrier,resource,subject), each object full policy then ALL. Never reduce the four relation booleans; owner proof remains independent AND. Fields never union across resources.
task_common_rules: Schema applies to internal canonical selectors, not a new public API DTO. All shown keys required after server default normalization; unknown keys rejected. IDs/filter values from request are locators only. Existing narrower domain validation still applies.

Every actual object uses full PDP decision including fields+scope from the same Grant; ALL objects required for whole artifacts and atomic writes, SQL row filtering for scoped lists. Never ANY/ALL aggregate relation flags across objects.
Read snapshot owns same Session+active REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY transaction, actor+Grants+parents+facts+projection. Only opaque snapshot proof permits skipping default actor SHARE.
Write batch takes complete domain topology locks then final user locks; callback does not acquire new domain locks or switch connection. Parent/object-set drift aborts/retries whole command.
PDP requests chunk at <=50 objects/resources using same observation and Grants; collect+strictly validate all chunks before publishing any decision/data. Chunk 2 failure invalidates chunk 1 allows.
All source-derived artifact bytes/report/history need whole-manifest and immutable generation coverage. Pending safe status is not empty successful provenance.
Receipt/event/accepted/applied replay is a fresh authorized read, not an unconditional idempotency escape. Historical NULL owner/provenance never guessed from username.

context_protocol.child_authorization_view_contract: Exact existing GET and command routes only, no new paths or generic resource/action parameters. Direct links must resolve without first reading another resource list. Authorized list rows may also carry child context but are not the only bootstrap. GET emits only its own fully resolved entry actions; command with changed/new parent or body targets uses its own zero-write authorization view before execute.

verified_empty_target_contract.trusted_only: Domain parser proves the complete actual selected target set is empty in this observation/locked plan. Nonempty source/upload with no parent, unresolved targets, pending job, absent owner or a page containing no rows is never an empty operation.
verified_empty_target_contract.admission: Always independently require current live explicit Grant/action/requires_fields/epoch/catalog. Empty ALL only skips individual target checks after named command admission. It never yields global facts/counters.
verified_empty_target_contract.business_semantics: This flag never relaxes existing business input validation; only the seven registered whole-target repair/recompute commands may return their existing no-op outcome.

context_protocol.core_entry_binding: Root typed EntryBinding contains exact entry_id, registered selected branch and full resolved slot set; compare against minimal runtime entry registry. Domain resolver supplies actual topology/owner proofs. Descriptive resource.allowed_context_kinds cannot authorize a call.

composite.admission: OR of the actual requested allow blocks; all-denied 403. Missing enabled canonical resource/runtime fault is whole 503. No fallback to legacy fields.

blocks.denied: project retains only stable supplied project_id locator; no descriptions, assignments or contract values
summary objects=null, reminders=[], counts=null; no underlying aggregation SQL
blocks.fields: Exact same-resource C/F guards, including ratio/status/colour/completeness/amount-derived signals. This intentionally grants aggregate HealthBand, never raw financial rows.

blocks.denied: project.contracts=[]; no contract row SQL; independent aggregate total can still exist under operation_summary
{rows:[],total:null,restricted:true}; same when own F absent because original full rows are financial; no expense row/count SQL

composite.block_access: Fixed block IDs above → S1 Decision. Only describes this projection, not a reusable Grant.
composite.workbook_preview: Structural sheet names/protocol may remain. overview.row_count is null unless contracts AND collection_snapshots allowed; site_requisitions row_count requires requisitions, approved_expenses requires its own allow+F, manager_tracking requires operation_summary. Denied totals never coerced to zero. It is not a file-download capability.
composite.not_a_block: No current top-level cost_gaps exists. maintenance_cost_fill.read_workspace may be retired from this entry unless implementation exposes a separately requested real diagnostic block; do not invoke it merely to obtain summary cost counts.
composite.revision: workbook_revision/data_version are business OCC, not authorization_revision; fingerprint never confers data rights.

binding_expression_NEVER_FLATTEN.additional_field_rules: Current own F controls financial columns. Supplying valuation retention ratio additionally requires adjust_valuation_parameters; never obtains fields from another resource.

internal_selector_contract.outer: ObjectRef.selector={purpose?:registeredPurpose, selection?:canonicalParameters}; children with no selector use {}
internal_selector_contract.schema_target: Each runtime slot.selector_schema validates selection only; purpose is checked separately against slot.purpose. Never accept client-authored trusted selector/proof.

context_protocol.display_contract: Display actions are module-level /me allow/deny switches. Context views carry only business data/mutation actions; surface requires show AND actual resource context. Never add show to object context requirements.

foundation_interfaces.parse_context_refs: parse_context_refs(db, identity, refs: Sequence[ObjectRef]) -> ContextBatch; trusted registered domain resolvers return actual carrier topology, per-resource policy subjects and revisions inside root-provided snapshot or complete write lock plan.
